Aa

Macrons

Consonantal i

Consonantal u

Theme

Civic life: news, government & the law

terms noun

of an agreement

also conditions, on these terms, under these conditions, terms of an agreement, stick by the terms, be on friendly terms with (a country)

classical

Liv. 2.13.4: hīs condiciōnibus compositā pāce (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 188

condiciōnēs, condiciōnum f. pl.

noun, third declension, plural

terms, conditions

Examples

  • hīs condiciōnibus

    on these terms, under these conditionsTraupman 184, 188; cf. Cic. Verr. 2.3.70 (Lewis & Short)

  • in condiciōnibus manēre

    to stick by the termsTraupman 188

  • in amīcitiā populī esse

    to be on friendly terms with a countryTraupman 188; cf. Nep. Hann. 2.4: esse in amīcitiā cum aliquō (Lewis & Short s.v. amīcitia)

See also propose, agreement, peace, treaty, condition.

SourcesLewis & Short: condicio · Lewis & Short: amicitia

John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 184, 188.

Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
